携手受信任的开发者与政府合作伙伴，有效提升生物防范能力 人工智能正加速推动生物学与生命科学的发展，为促进科学突破、强化公共卫生体系以及提升应对生物威胁的韧性带来了全新的可能。随着这些能力日益强大，致力于预防、检测和应对生物威胁的机构同样需要更为出色的工具。我们坚信，前沿 AI 应当切实为这些防御者提供优势。而要做到这一点，需要负责任的部署机制与受信任的访问模式，从而将这些先进能力交到通过审核的合作伙伴手中，由他们构建全新的生物防御应用、工具和方案，以增强社会韧性。 因此，我们今天宣布采取两项新举措，以加速生物学领域的防御能力建设： 启动 Rosalind 生物防御计划，以帮助受信任的开发者构建全新的生物防御与大流行病防范能力。点击此处申请。 扩大 GPT‑Rosalind 的受信任访问范围，向支持公共卫生和生物防御任务的特定美国政府及盟友合作伙伴开放。在此申请访问权限。 我们今天采取的这些步骤，是一项更广泛战略的一部分，旨在确保前沿 AI 能切实为那些致力于预防、检测和应对生物威胁的工作人员提供助力。该战略包括：通过让防御者获得受信任的先进 AI 工具访问权限来为其赋能；加速医疗反制措施的开发；构建更早的预警系统；加强诊断、应急准备和响应能力；以及支持建立一个稳健的评估生态系统。在未来的几周内，我们将继续分享我们在这些领域的更多工作进展。 随着 AI 模型在生物学领域的能力日益提升，我们一直致力于确保这些能力的部署既能推动科学进步，又能强化安全防线。我们的方法侧重于构建多层韧性：对防备评测进行投入、开展生物领域专属的能力评估、针对双用途生物学请求优化模型的安全行为、实施监测与合规审查、引入专家红队测试，并针对高风险能力部署安全控制措施。 2025 年 7 月，我们发布了 ChatGPT 智能体，这是我们在准备框架 (Preparedness Framework)下首个定义为“生物学高能力”的模型，并为此启用了强有力的安全防护措施，以最大程度降低危害风险。自那时起，随着模型能力的不断演进，我们持续优化这些防护措施，并分享了详细的评估报告⁠（在新窗口中打开）。同时，我们继续与外部测试团队在部署前评估方面保持紧密合作，他们的发现有助于验证并完善我们的方法。 此外，我们还与外部专家及公共部门合作伙伴紧密联手，共同强化更广泛的生物安全生态系统，合作伙伴包括资深生物学家、美国 AI 标准与创新研究所 (CAISI) 和英国 AI 安全研究所 (UK AISI) 等政府机构、洛斯阿拉莫斯国家实验室以及前沿模型论坛 (Frontier Model Forum)。今天的发布立足于前期成果，进一步扩大受信任合作伙伴使用GPT‑Rosalind开展高影响力防御应用的途径。这一举措既为研发新型反制措施的防御者提供支持，也向承担公共卫生与生物防御任务的政府伙伴扩展受信任的访问权限。 通过 Rosalind 生物防御计划加速防御能力建设 加速防御能力建设的核心，是确保前沿 AI 能力能够切实赋能那些构建社会防线的群体。为了帮助受信任的开发者将前沿能力转化为实际的防御手段，我们正式启动了 Rosalind 生物防御计划。这是一项全新的倡议，旨在利用 GPT‑Rosalind（我们专为生命科学研究打造的前沿推理模型），推动 AI 在生命科学领域的高影响力防御应用开发。 该计划旨在帮助受信任的开发者将前沿 AI 能力应用于具有操作性的生物防御工具中，从而在生物威胁出现之前强化防备。OpenAI 将资助 GPT‑Rosalind 的访问额度，并为那些构建前沿生物安全应用、旨在巩固社会防线，并打造大流行病防备能力的受信任开发者提供启动支持。这涵盖了流行病学建模、早期检测、筛查、应急准备、非药物干预 (NPI) 以及其他与公共卫生相关的能力领域。 在启动阶段，我们正为首批利用 GPT‑Rosalind 在生物防御全栈领域构建前沿应用的机构提供支持。它们的工作贯穿了生物威胁的全生命周期：从预防、早期检测到社会韧性以及医疗反制措施的开发。这些实践有助于展示前沿 AI 如何辅助公共卫生团队、研究人员、基础设施运营商以及社区，共同防范无论是自然发生还是人工合成的生物风险。 Fourth Eon Biosecurity 致力于构建能够与 AI 等新技术同步演进的自适应筛查基础设施。该机构从基于功能的 DNA 合成筛查入手，协助处理生物材料的实验室和企业拦截不安全或恶意的订单，其中包括涉及新型设计的订单。 我们的目标不仅是在抽象层面上加速生命科学研究，更是为了助力创造出能够增强社会韧性的产品与干预手段，并展示负责任、高影响力的生物防御在实践中究竟如何落地。我们对那些先进 AI 能够切实提升防御研究工作流速度、质量或规模的项目尤为感兴趣，包括文献综述、实验方案设计支持、模型构建、数据协调、模拟、决策支持和科学传播。我们欢迎来自学术界、非营利组织、政府附属机构、使命驱动型企业以及其他符合条件且项目涉及明确公共利益的研究团队提交申请。 强化生物防范能力需要一个由众多防御者构成的广泛生态系统。除了支持开发新型防御应用的受信任构建者外，我们还在向那些在预防、检测和应对生物威胁中发挥核心作用的公共机构扩大访问权限。今天，我们正式向特定承担已获批公共卫生和生物防御任务的美国政府及盟友合作伙伴，扩展 GPT‑Rosalind 的受信任访问权限。此举旨在让符合条件的团队将前沿 AI 应用于高影响力的工作流中，例如早期预警系统、疫情响应规划、诊断、应急准备以及医疗反制措施的开发。 在保护社区、将科学证据转化为行动，以及为新出现的生物挑战做好准备方面，政府公共卫生机构和研究组织发挥着至关重要的作用。通过受信任访问模式扩大访问范围，我们可以协助符合条件的团队将 GPT‑Rosalind 用于具有明确益处的防御工作，同时维持与先进生物能力相匹配的安全、防范及问责控制措施。 这一扩展举措体现了我们更为广泛的方法理念：在提升强大工具可及性的同时，部署相应的安全防护措施，并对整个生态系统的韧性进行持续投入。强大的社会防备能力有赖于政府、研究机构、行业，以及技术提供商之间的通力合作。向符合条件的公共卫生与科学合作伙伴开放 GPT‑Rosalind，是帮助该生态系统更高效地开展准备、响应和防御工作的重要一步。 劳伦斯利弗莫尔国家实验室 (LLNL) 正在应用 AI 来推进生物防备与生物韧性工作。LLNL 的工作融合了 AI、超级计算、先进模拟以及实验室检测，旨在支持针对新兴生物威胁的潜在医疗反制措施的设计与评估。其目标是提高防备能力、加速响应速度，并增强开发有效反制措施的信心。 劳伦斯利弗莫尔国家实验室 (LLNL) 正在应用 AI 来推进生物防备与生物韧性工作。LLNL 的工作融合了 AI、超级计算、先进模拟以及实验室检测，旨在支持针对新兴生物威胁的潜在医疗反制措施的设计与评估。其目标是提高防备能力、加速响应速度，并增强开发有效反制措施的信心。 同时，我们也在与约翰斯·霍普金斯大学应用物理实验室展开合作，该实验室计划将 GPT‑Rosalind 整合到蛋白质工程平台中，以加速用于治疗、反制措施开发以及新兴生物威胁特征分析的突变酶筛查。此外，我们正向流行病防范创新联盟 (CEPI) 开放 GPT‑Rosalind 的访问权限，该联盟正专注于其“100 天任务”(100 Days Mission)，旨在加速针对流行病和大流行病威胁（包括当前的埃博拉疫情）的疫苗开发。 今天的发布只是我们更广泛愿景的初步尝试 — 即利用 GPT‑Rosalind 全面赋能公共卫生、生物防御和生命科学研究。Rosalind 生物防御计划面向全球符合条件的申请者开放，我们期待支持更多构建防御应用的机构，利用 GPT‑Rosalind 来提升社会韧性。 随着时间的推移，我们也期望继续扩大受信任的政府合作伙伴与 GPT‑Rosalind 的协作方式。通过从首批部署中汲取经验，并继续与美国及海外的合作伙伴深化对话，我们将持续优化所需的访问路径、支持的模型和安全防护措施，以协助符合条件的机构负责任地使用前沿生命科学 AI。

Memory sources aren't shown to others if you choose to share a chat. You remain in control of what's in your memory: you can delete chats you no longer want to be cited, delete or change items in saved memories in settings, or use temporary chats that don't use or update your memory. Starting with GPT‑5.1, our models began developing a strange habit: they increasingly mentioned goblins, gremlins, and other creatures in their metaphors. Unlike model bugs that show up through a tanking eval or a spiking training metric and point back to a specific change, this one crept in subtly. A single “little goblin” in an answer could be harmless, even charming. Across model generations, though, the habit became hard to miss: the goblins kept multiplying, and we needed to figure out where they came from. In early testing, GPT‑5.5 in Codex showed an odd affinity for goblin metaphors. The short answer is that model behavior is shaped by many small incentives. In this case, one of those incentives came from training the model for thepersonality customization feature⁠(opens in a new window), in particular the Nerdy personality. We unknowingly gave particularly high rewards for metaphors with creatures. From there, the goblins spread. The goblins were funny at first, but the increasing number of employee reports became concerning. An interesting interaction our Chief Scientist had with GPT‑5.5. The first signs of creatures The first time we clearly saw the pattern was in November, after the GPT‑5.1 launch,although it may have started earlier⁠(opens in a new window). Users complained about the model being oddly overfamiliar in conversation, which prompted an investigation into specific verbal tics. A safety researcher had experienced a few “goblins” and “gremlins” and asked that they be included in the check. When we looked, use of “goblin” in ChatGPT had risen by 175% after the launch of GPT‑5.1, while “gremlin” had risen by 52%. A measurable small lexical quirk in GPT‑5.1. At the time, the prevalence of goblins did not look especially alarming. A few months later, the goblins came back to haunt us in a much more specific and reproducible form. Solving the goblin mystery With GPT‑5.4, weand our users⁠(opens in a new window)noticed an even bigger uptick in references to these creatures. That triggered another internal analysis and surfaced the first connection to the root cause: creature language was especially common in production traffic from users who had selected the “Nerdy” personality. “Nerdy” used the following system prompt, which partially explained the quirkiness: You are an unapologetically nerdy, playful and wise AI mentor to a human. You are passionately enthusiastic about promoting truth, knowledge, philosophy, the scientific method, and critical thinking. [...] You must undercut pretension through playful use of language. The world is complex and strange, and its strangeness must be acknowledged, analyzed, and enjoyed. Tackle weighty subjects without falling into the trap of self-seriousness. [...] If the behavior were simply a broad internet trend, we would expect it to spread more evenly. Instead, it was clustered in the part of the system explicitly optimized for a playful, nerdy style. Nerdy accounted for only 2.5% of all ChatGPT responses, but 66.7% of all “goblin” mentions in ChatGPT responses. The behavior was highly concentrated in the "Nerdy" personality. Because “goblin” prevalence seemed to increase over our model releases, we had a suspicion that something in our personality instruction-following training was amplifying this. Codex helped us compare model outputs generated during RL training containing goblin or gremlin with outputs from the same task that did not. One reward signal stood out immediately: the one originally designed to encourage the Nerdy personality was consistently more favorable to the creature-word outputs. Across all datasets in the audit, the Nerdy personality reward showed a clear tendency to score outputs to the same problem with “goblin” or “gremlin” higher than outputs without, with positive uplift in 76.2% of datasets. That explained why the behavior was boosted with the Nerdy personality prompt, but not why it also appeared without that prompt. To test whether the style was transferring, we tracked mention rates over training both with and without the Nerdy prompt. As goblin and gremlin mentions increased under the Nerdy personality, they increased by nearly the same relative proportion in samples without it. Taken together, the evidence suggests that the broader behavior emerged through transfer from Nerdy personality training. The rewards were applied only in the Nerdy condition, but reinforcement learning does not guarantee that learned behaviors stay neatly scoped to the condition that produced them. Once a style tic is rewarded, later training can spread or reinforce it elsewhere, especially if those outputs are reused in supervised fine-tuning or preference data. That creates a feedback loop: Playful style is rewarded Some rewarded examples contain a distinctive lexical tic. The tic appears more often in rollouts. Model-generated rollouts are used for supervised fine-tuning (SFT). The model gets even more comfortable producing the tic. A search through GPT‑5.5’s SFT data found many datapoints containing “goblin” and “gremlin.” Further investigation revealed a whole family of other odd creatures: raccoons, trolls, ogres, and pigeons were identified as other tic words, while most uses of frog turned out to be legitimate. One week average of production prevalence of goblins and gremlins. The drop in GPT‑5.4 Thinking was a result of retiring the “Nerdy” personality mid-March. GPT‑5.5 never launched with the “Nerdy” personality, and showed another increase over GPT‑5.4 (even without “Nerdy”). The end of the goblins We retired the “Nerdy” personality in March after launching GPT‑5.4. In training, we removed the goblin-affine reward signal and filtered training data containing creature-words, making goblins less likely to over-appear or show up in inappropriate contexts. Unfortunately, GPT‑5.5 started training before we found the root cause of the goblins. When we began testing GPT‑5.5 in Codex, OpenAI employees immediately noticed the strange affinity for goblins, and we added adeveloper-prompt instruction⁠(opens in a new window)to mitigate. Codex is, after all, quite nerdy. If you want to let the creatures run free in Codex, you can run this command to launch Codex with the goblin-suppressing instructions removed: Depending on who you ask, the goblins are a delightful or annoying quirk of the model. But they are also a powerful example of how reward signals can shape model behavior in unexpected ways, and how models can learn to generalize rewards in certain situations to unrelated ones. Taking the time to understand why a model is behaving in a strange way, and building out ways to investigate those patterns quickly, is an important capability for our research team. This investigation resulted in new tools for the research team to audit model behavior and fix behavior problems at their root.

GPT‑5.5 is a new model designed for complex, real-world work, including writing code, researching online, analyzing information, creating documents and spreadsheets, and moving across tools to get things done. Relative to earlier models, GPT‑5.5 understands the task earlier, asks for less guidance, uses tools more effectively, checks it work and keeps going until it’s done. We subjected the model to our full suite of predeployment safety evaluations and our Preparedness Framework, including targeted red-teaming for advanced cybersecurity and biology capabilities, and collected feedback on real use cases from nearly 200 early-access partners before release. We are releasing GPT‑5.5 with our strongest set of safeguards to date, designed to reduce misuse while preserving legitimate, beneficial uses of advanced capabilities. We generally treat GPT‑5.5’s safety results as strong proxies for GPT‑5.5 Pro, which is the same underlying model using a setting that makes use of parallel test time compute. As noted below, we separately evaluate GPT‑5.5 Pro in certain cases because we judge that the setting could materially impact the relevant risks or appropriate safeguards posture. Except where noted, the results in system cards describe evaluations we ran in an offline setting. This card was updated on April 24, 2026, to include additional information about safeguards for the deployment of GPT‑5.5 and GPT‑5.5 Pro in the API. Global AffairsJun 2, 2026

制定的方案更有信心，且极少需要对具体实现进行人工修正。 一位提前试用该模型的 NVIDIA 工程师感叹道：“失去对 GPT‑5.5 的访问权限，感觉就像被截肢了一样。” 这些让 GPT‑5.5 在编程领域大放异彩的优势，同样使其成为日常办公的强大助力。由于模型能更敏锐地捕捉用户意向，它在处理知识型工作时显得更加自然流畅：从搜集资料、提炼核心价值，到调用工具、核查产出，并最终将零散的素材转化为实用成果，整个链路一气呵成。 在 Codex 环境下，GPT‑5.5 制作文档、表格及演示文稿的能力较 GPT‑5.4 有了显著提升。Alpha
